title: LandlordGuard Renewal Term Premium: Pricing Rule and Worked Figures
content:
**Rule.** The renewal term premium of a LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy is the smaller of the indicated renewal premium on the policy and the expiring term premium increased by the renewal cap percentage (that capped figure rounded half-up to the cent), and that smaller figure is then increased by the account adjustment percentage, reduced by the flat account credit and rounded half-up to the cent.

The standard renewal cap percentage is the tier's renewal rate cap, the standard account adjustment percentage is zero and the standard flat account credit is zero.

## How the figures fit together

1. **Capped figure** — the expiring term premium multiplied by one hundred plus the renewal cap percentage, divided by one hundred, rounded half-up to the cent at this point.
2. **Smaller figure** — the lower of the indicated renewal premium recorded on the policy and the capped figure. The cap never raises a premium: when the indicated renewal premium is the lower, it stands.
3. **Account adjustment** — the smaller figure multiplied by one hundred plus the account adjustment percentage, divided by one hundred.
4. **Flat account credit** — taken off after the account adjustment.
5. **Rounding** — the result is rounded half-up to the cent once more, at the end.

## Worked figures (hypothetical policies, renewal cap taken as 15 percent unless stated)

| Expiring term premium | Capped figure | Indicated renewal premium on the policy | Smaller figure | Renewal term premium |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,700.00 | 1,955.00 | 1,980.00 | 1,955.00 | 1,955.00 |
| 1,700.00 | 1,955.00 | 1,900.00 | 1,900.00 | 1,900.00 |
| 1,111.11 (cap taken as 12 percent) | 1,244.44 | 1,300.00 | 1,244.44 | 1,244.44 |

In the third row 1,111.11 multiplied by 112 and divided by 100 is 1,244.4432, rounded half-up to 1,244.44 before the comparison.
